svg.title: Which Query Engine? Spark SQL vs SQL Analytics Endpoint vs Warehouse T-SQL vs KQL
svg.desc: Fabric query engine decision matrix: Compare Spark SQL in notebooks, Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint, Synapse Warehouse T-SQL, and Eventhouse KQL across language, read/write capabilities, underlying compute architecture, and anti-patterns.
svg.text: Which Query Engine? Spark SQL vs SQL Endpoint vs Warehouse vs KQL
Workload selection matrix: Read/write permissions, developer skillset, transaction semantics, and telemetry latency

g.aria-label: What does the query workload need?
g.title: What does the query workload need? — The root question: read/write need, skillset, and data shape decide the engine.
g.text: 1. Read vs Write: Does the workload need to mutate Delta tables (CREATE, INSERT, MERGE, DELETE) or perform read-only querying?
2. Developer Context: Data engineering notebook with PySpark/Scala vs BI / Reporting tool (SSMS, Power BI) vs Streaming Telemetry?
3. Data Shape: Relational / tabular Delta Lake vs High-volume, append-only time-series events requiring sub-second KQL aggregations?

g.title: Spark SQL (notebook cell) — Spark-native, read/write, shares the notebook's Spark session — pick this for transformation workloads.
g.text: Catalyst + AQE + Native Velox SIMD C++

g.title: Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint — Read-only T-SQL over lakehouse Delta tables — pick this for ad hoc BI-style querying, never writes.
Warehouse T-SQL — Full governed T-SQL with multi-table ACID transactions — pick this when the workload writes and needs transactional semantics.
KQL against Eventhouse — High-volume time-series/telemetry querying — pick this when the data shape is streaming or log data, not relational.
g.text: SSD hot cache + OneLake delta availability.

g.aria-label: Trap: SQL analytics endpoint is read-only
g.title: Trap: SQL analytics endpoint is read-only — Attempting to write through the SQL analytics endpoint fails — it looks like a normal SQL surface but isn't.
g.text: The SQL Analytics Endpoint is Strictly Read-Only
• Common Mistake: Connecting an ETL pipeline or app to the Lakehouse SQL endpoint and attempting INSERT, UPDATE, or CREATE TABLE.
• Consequence: The operation will immediately fail. Although it exposes standard TDS / T-SQL, it contains no write engine.
• Architectural Solution: If your pipeline requires T-SQL writes with ACID transactions, provision a Warehouse; if using notebooks, write via Spark SQL.

svg.text: Fabric Atlas — Original Diagram, August 2026. Grounded in Microsoft Fabric Multi-Engine Architecture documentation.
